clue.text: Maiden, say, as sailor, big achiever

blocks.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
e.g. means 'for example', i.e. say
taken as written
a tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A list of comparisons: a maiden, a sailor, someone who achieves great things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is the familiar crossword way to clue EG, as in for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A megastar is an extremely famous performer, someone whose success is huge.

clue.text: Mum joins church club

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A mother signing up to a church social group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a society to join, but it is the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a heavy medieval weapon with a spiked head, a kind of cudgel.

clue.text: End of trying — I have to yield

indicators.note: end of picks out only the closing letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: the final letter of trying
the contraction I've

explanation.surface: Someone at the end of their efforts admitting they must surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: To give is to bend or collapse under pressure, the same as yield.

clue.text: Great sites for redevelopment according to schemes

indicators.note: redevelopment means rebuilding, so the letters are torn down and put back differently

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Planning documents earmark excellent plots for regeneration.
explanation.definitionFit: Strategies are plans of action designed to achieve a goal, another word for schemes.

clue.text: Learner is bad, coming out with impromptu comments

indicators.note: coming out suggests emerging in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: L is the learner driver's plate
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A poor student blurting out unscripted remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad libs are remarks improvised on the spot, not written or rehearsed beforehand.

clue.text: Objections about this fag end?

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word it governs is read from right to left

blocks.note: 'buts' are objections, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Someone raising objections about a cigarette butt.
explanation.walkthrough: A fag is British slang for a cigarette, so the fag end is the stub left after smoking it.
explanation.definitionFit: The short remaining piece of a smoked cigarette is called its stub, a leftover stump.

clue.text: Vessel in good condition managed to support area

blocks.note: trim means neat and in good order
A is the abbreviation for area
ran as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A ship kept shipshape and run so as to back up a region.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue one piece supporting another sits beneath it, so the word for managed goes under the abbreviation for area.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimaran is a sailing boat with three parallel hulls, a type of vessel.

clue.text: They may provide support for librarians

definitions.text: They may provide support for librarians

blocks.clueFragment: They may provide support for librarians
blocks.note: surface reading: people who help or back up library staff
setter's reading: physical props that hold up the volumes on a librarian's shelves

explanation.walkthrough: Support sounds like help for the staff; it is the literal holding upright of rows of volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: These are heavy supports placed at each end of a row of volumes to keep them standing upright.

clue.text: Maiden maybe in request for a large blanket?

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the word for the request

blocks.note: a call is a request, as in a call for help
a maiden is one kind of over in cricket: six balls with no runs scored

explanation.surface: Asking for a big blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: a really big blanket would cover everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A coverall is something that covers every part, so a huge throw spread over everything fits loosely.

clue.text: Artist using mud mostly and egg!

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: mire is mud, shortened by its last letter
an egg is round like the letter O, which is also a duck (nought) in cricket

explanation.surface: A painter working with mud and egg, as in tempera.
explanation.walkthrough: Egg tempera is a real painting medium, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan Miró was a Spanish surrealist painter and sculptor of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Animal not heartless, having earlier been awfully kind

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so these letters come out in a mangled order
without its heart a word keeps only its outer letters, its middle removed

blocks.note: the letters of been, rearranged
a vole is a small rodent
the first and last letters of not

explanation.surface: An animal that was once cruel but now has a heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having earlier' tells you the jumbled been comes before the animal and the shortened not.
explanation.definitionFit: Benevolent describes someone well-meaning and generous, wishing good to others.

clue.text: Fellow competitor running ablest team

indicators.note: running can mean operating or in motion, so the letters are set moving into a new order

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rival in a race lining up the most able team.
explanation.definitionFit: A stablemate is a horse trained in the same yard, and by extension a colleague who also competes.

clue.text: Hesitant to admit boy as domestic servant?

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one word takes the other inside it

blocks.note: chary means wary or reluctant
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone unsure about taking a boy on as household help.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlady is a British cleaning woman who does housework for pay, a kind of household help.

clue.text: Lively male wearing coarse cloth

indicators.note: wearing places one piece inside another, like a body inside clothes

blocks.note: sacking is rough cloth used for sacks
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A sprightly man dressed in sackcloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A smacking breeze or pace is brisk and vigorous, full of energy.

clue.text: Silver in residence maybe what the lord’s demanded?

indicators.note: in puts the metal inside the word for a dwelling

blocks.note: a home is one example of a residence
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A lord asking for the family silver kept at his house.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal times a vassal had to pay formal homage, a public acknowledgement of allegiance, to his lord.

clue.text: See what’s in Hampshire garden

indicators.note: what's in points to letters sitting inside the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the county and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: An invitation to look at a garden in Hampshire, a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to look at it or consider it, a formal synonym of observe.

clue.text: Gas, more than enough? That’s too much!

indicators.note: the cry says the phrase has more letters than needed, so only a run inside it is wanted

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word, all of the second, and the first of the third

explanation.surface: Complaining that there is an excess of gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethane is a colourless hydrocarbon gas found in natural gas deposits.

clue.text: Engineers getting something made for play

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a creation is anything produced or made

explanation.surface: Engineers building a toy or game.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreation means leisure activity and amusement, time spent having fun rather than working.

clue.text: Girl leading a fete?

blocks.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman in charge of a village fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive public occasion, like a fete or carnival.

clue.text: Gregory’s kiss?

blocks.note: first meaning: the surname of the Hollywood actor Gregory
second meaning: a quick light kiss

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a film star's kiss; the actor's surname and the small kiss are the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor Gregory Peck starred in Roman Holiday, and a quick brief kiss on the cheek is also called by this word.

clue.text: A king getting in close

blocks.note: taken as written; that the answer also runs across the words 'A king' is a coincidence, as the setter's parse is A, K, IN
K is the chess abbreviation for king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch being admitted to somewhere nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Akin means closely related or similar, so two things that are akin are close in nature.

clue.text: Watch out! Ignoring article, Pinter play cycling without end

indicators.note: ignoring a word for 'the' means the title loses its opening definite article
without its end the word loses its final letter
cycling moves letters round from the front to the back, like a wheel turning

blocks.note: The Caretaker is a 1960 play by Harold Pinter

explanation.surface: A warning shouted during a revival of a Pinter play.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop THE and the final R to leave CARETAKE, then move CARE from the front to the back to get TAKE CARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Take care is a warning phrase urging caution, just like watch out.

clue.text: Exercises for body and soul? Unknown in the past, going back

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: ago means in the past, as in long ago
x, y and z are the unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: A mysterious regime nobody had heard of in olden days.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoga is a discipline of postures and breathing intended to train both physical and spiritual health.

clue.text: Felt awkward joining financial outfit in area of Paris

indicators.note: awkward suggests something clumsy and out of place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of felt, rearranged
a bank is a financial institution

explanation.surface: Feeling uncomfortable on joining a Paris bank.
explanation.definitionFit: The Left Bank is the southern side of the Seine in Paris, famous for artists and cafés.
